one_month_reasoning: In-window events (to 2026-10-30): (1) FOMC Oct 27-28, after the Sep 17 hike to a 4.00% upper bound with the 10-year at 5.24%; another hike would pressure long-duration AI-infrastructure multiples, a hold would relieve them. (2) Peer Q3 prints: Vertiv ~Oct 28 (est., Q3 guide ~$3.75B revenue, EPS ~$1.80), Schneider Q3 revenue late October, GE Vernova, Hubbell, nVent, Wesco. For the read-across to be positive they need data-center orders/backlog still growing y/y against tough comps and no guide trims; given Q2 raises, NEMA EBCI current conditions rising to 65.8 in August (from 63.0), and management's Laguna comment that Q3 is 'very strong', a supportive read is somewhat more likely than not. (3) Hyperscaler Q3 results in late October with 2027 capex commentary. (4) Eaton's own Q3 report: Nov 3 is an unconfirmed aggregator estimate; Eaton reported Q3 on Oct 31 in 2023 and 2024, so ~25-30% odds it lands inside the window, a mildly positive but mostly variance-adding event. Net: two-sided event risk, so I stay close to symmetric: median ~$433 (a hair above spot on supportive chain data, offset by rate risk) with ~11.5% monthly vol (39%/3.5 plus a small bump for the event-dense window).

fair_value.method: Both legs now price the horizon on NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) pro-forma ex-Mobility EPS of ~$16.7 on ~381M post-split-off shares: 26x standalone multiple with a rate haircut = $434 (60%), and a Schneider-anchored 27x peer multiple = $451 (40%); blended ~$441.

$15.6 x 389.5M = ~$6.08B net income, less ~$340M Mobility, plus ~$40M after-tax interest saved on $1.1B debt repaid = ~$5.78B / ~381.5M shares = ~$15.15.

$15.2 grown ~13%: Electrical Americas backlog +33%, Electrical Global +103%, DC orders +85%; peers still raising (Vertiv organic ~31%, Schneider 10-13%, Hubbell DC +65%, nVent +47%); NEMA EBCI current conditions 65.8 in Aug. Growth tapers from 2027 as hyperscaler capex growth slows into 2028.
ETN ~27.7x 2027 consensus today; Schneider forward ~24-30x. Growth decelerating to low-teens and a 5.24% 10-year / Fed hiking argue against re-rating; 26x is a modest de-rate.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: Same NTM pro-forma EPS ~$16.7 x 27x peer-anchored multiple (Schneider band midpoint)

inputs_detail.derivation: Schneider forward ~24-30x (midpoint ~27); Vertiv 40x+ is a pure-play ceiling. ETN post-Mobility is more data-center/grid weighted (premium) but carries ~$20B net debt with no 2026 buybacks and faces a higher-rate backdrop (discount); net ~27x, down from 28x in round 1.

bear.story: AI-capex digestion becomes real: hyperscalers temper 2027-28 builds, peer (Vertiv/Schneider/GEV) data-center orders turn negative on tough comps, ETN pro-forma 2027 EPS ~$14.5 and NTM ~$15.5, multiple compresses to ~19-20x with the 10-year above 5%.

base.story: Chain demand holds (2027 hyperscaler capex ~$0.9-1T, transformer capacity booked through Q3 2027, record backlogs); Q3 margin step-up delivered; Mobility split-off closes Q1 2027 retiring ~8M shares with $1.1B to debt; NTM pro-forma EPS ~$16.9 x ~26.5x.

bull.story: 2027 capex >$1T, ETN share gains in DC power/liquid cooling (Boyd), price/cost tailwind in 2027 lifts NTM EPS to ~$18.5 and the market keeps ~30x despite rates.

thesis_break_reason: About $330 (~-24%, near the 52-week low zone) is ~20x pro-forma ex-Mobility NTM EPS (~$16.7), consistent only with estimates being cut: hyperscaler capex reductions or data-center order cancellations visible in ETN's and peers' (Vertiv, Schneider, Hubbell, nVent) orders/backlog, not just sentiment or rate de-rating.

key_uncertainties: Durability of hyperscaler capex into 2027-28 (Moody's/sell-side ~$0.9-1T in 2027, growth slowing in 2028)
Rates: Fed hiking and a 5.24% 10-year versus a ~27x multiple
Q3 segment-margin step-up of ~170bp after the Q1 guide cut to 24.1-24.5% (Boyd/Ultra PCS mix)
Split-off take-up: undersubscription would trigger a clean-up pro-rata distribution and fewer shares retired
Competition from Schneider/Vertiv/ABB/Siemens in DC power and liquid cooling
reasoning: Round 2 changes: the supervisor established from Eaton's Form 425 and Q2 10-Q that the Mobility/Dana deal is a split-off by exchange offer (I called it a spin), the $1.1B cash goes to capital allocation including debt repayment (not buybacks), and Eaton will do no buybacks in 2026; I confirmed the exchange-offer structure and Q1 2027 close from Eaton's 8-K/release. Rebuilding dilution: ~$340M after-tax Mobility profit lost, ~$40M interest saved, ~8M shares retired, gives 2027 pro-forma EPS ~$15.2 (vs ~$15.6 consensus incl. Mobility), i.e. ~3%, more than the $0.3-0.4 I had. I also add the rate backdrop I ignored (Fed hike Sep 17, 10-year 5.24%), which trims my peer multiple from 28x to 27x, and I fix my second leg to price NTM EPS at the horizon instead of 2027 EPS. I drop the Manifold market (resolved N/A, 39 trades). Lane evidence since round 1 is slightly positive: NEMA EBCI current conditions rose to 65.8 in August from 63.0, respondents citing data-center and grid orders; Vertiv guides Q3 revenue ~$3.75B; Moody's raised hyperscaler capex forecasts toward ~$1T by 2027; transformer capacity is reported booked through Q3 2027. Fair value falls from $445 to ~$441 (NTM $16.7 x 26x = $434 at 60%, x 27x = $451 at 40%), essentially spot. Scenario mean ~$450 (bear $300/20%, base $450/55%, bull $570/25%). The ladder is a mixture: 85% lognormal with median $447 and 31% vol, plus 15% capex-digestion tail with median $365 and 40% vol, giving an overall median ~$434 and P(>=432) 0.51 (down from 0.545). I keep an independent view from the supervisor on multiple (26-27x still defensible given low-teens EPS growth and chain order data). What would move me: peer Q3 data-center orders falling y/y (down), or an FOMC hold plus hyperscaler 2027 capex guides of >$1T (up). Research this round was limited to 4 searches.
